sentences.text: Pinacosuchus is a small crocodylomorph, a group of reptiles related to modern crocodiles, known for its unique spiky dermal armor.
Its protective suit included five distinct types of scutes, ranging from simple rectangles to elongate pointed spines.
The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — includes a sacrum measuring only 14.3 mm in length.
The genus was named by Gilmore in 1942, with the type species designated as Pinacosuchus mantiensis.
Fossils were found in the Late Cretaceous North Horn Formation of Utah, specifically at the "Lizard Locality" within the Manti National Forest.
Gilmore determined the specimen was an adult based on the absence of sutures on the neural arches of the vertebrae.
This animal lived during the Late Cretaceous period, specifically between 72.2 and 66 million years ago in the Maastrichtian stage.
